title: VPC post-deploy quick-verify: API handshake and model instantiation pressure test
creator: Maya Chen
description: Objective: Add a compact, automatable verification job that runs immediately after a VPC/private deployment completes. This job must confirm API endpoint reachability, model process instantiation under light-to-moderate pressure, a small set of deterministic inference checks, and a clear pass/fail signal to the deployment pipeline. The goal is a fast (<6m) gate that detects configuration or runtime failures not caught by terraform apply and system-level checks.
acceptance_criteria: Job runs as part of post-deploy stage in private deployment pipeline and returns explicit success/failure status
API health check: TLS handshake + /v1/health + token-auth verification within 2s from the private network
Model instantiation: each GPU node can load a reference model binary within 90s under CI resource constraints
Inference sanity: 3 deterministic prompts return expected structure and no runtime errors
Resource signals: CPU, GPU memory, and kv-cache metrics reported back to console for the timeframe of the run
On failure, pipeline marks deployment as failed and attaches logs + suggested remediation steps
runbook_steps: Step 1 - API handshake: curl --retry 2 -sSf -m 5 https://<private-endpoint>/v1/health with svc token and verify 200 and JSON {"status":"ready"}
Step 2 - Auth check: exchange service token via token-introspect endpoint and validate claims (uid, roles)
Step 3 - Model instantiation pressure test: run lightweight loader that sequentially requests model init on 2 pods with 30s gap; capture timing and errors
Step 4 - Deterministic inference: send 3 small prompts (summarize tiny snippet, identity echo, and embedding spot-check) and validate outputs against golden regexes
Step 5 - Metrics snapshot: collect top-level metrics (gpu_util, gpu_mem_used, process_rss, kv_cache_hits) for 2 minutes and upload to deployment artifact store
Step 6 - Post-check analysis: if any step fails, collect /var/log/redwood/*.log, system journal, and the loader process trace and attach to pipeline failure
test_cases: TC-1 API-handshake-success: expect 200 + status ready + latency < 2s
TC-2 Auth-expiry-safeguard: invalid token returns 401 and appropriate audit event
TC-3 Model-load-serial: model binary loads on node A and node B within configured timeout (<=90s)
TC-4 Inference-echo: prompt 'REDWOOD_CHECK_42' returns response containing 'REDWOOD_CHECK_42' within 2 tokens of beginning
TC-5 Embedding-length: embedding vector length matches model spec and no NaNs
implementation_notes: Prefer a light-weight Go binary for the loader/test runner to avoid Python runtime variance in private images
Leverage existing terraform output keys: private_api_endpoint, deployment_token_secret_id, and node_pool_tags
Add a CI job 'vpc-quick-verify' that can be invoked by the deploy pipeline and run in ephemeral runner inside customer's VPC via bastion or controller agent
Store golden regexes and small fixture prompts in infra repo under infra/vpc/checks/ for ease of updates
Expose a per-run artifact URL in the pipeline UI linking to the metrics snapshot and logs
automation_tasks: Add terraform null_resource that triggers the verification job as the final step (or invoke pipeline)
Create k8s job manifest for the loader and a sidecar that captures logs to a PVC
Implement Go runner: flags for endpoint, token, model-name, and run-timeout; output JSON result to stdout
Add GH Action or internal CI workflow 'vpc-quick-verify' and wire it into private deploy pipeline templates
Add lightweight console alert mapping for failed verification runs to surface in the deployment dashboard

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Running the loader can cause OOM on small private nodes. Mitigation: default to conservative concurrency (1 at a time) and a configurable memory cap flag.
Risk: False positives due to transient network flakiness. Mitigation: add short retry/backoff in API handshake and require persistent failure over 2 attempts to fail the job.
Risk: Sensitive tokens being logged. Mitigation: redact token values in logs and rely on ephemeral token exchange; require SRE sign-off for exceptions.
Risk: Test maintenance overhead as models change. Mitigation: keep fixtures minimal and validate only structural outputs (regex/golden keys) rather than full text match
